m1.name: widget.add
m1.summary: Add ONE widget of a given type to the Charts workspace, placed automatically in empty space. Use one op per widget.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the workspace entry. "as" NAMES THE NEW WIDGET: if any later op in this plan changes the new widget (a new chart's symbol, timeframe, …), set "as" to a short unique name (new1, new2, …) and use exactly that name as those ops' target — a later op may not target a new widget whose "as" is null. Otherwise "as" is null. Example: "add 2 charts on SPY and QQQ" → widget.add{type:chart, as:"new1"}, widget.add{type:chart, as:"new2"}, chart.setSymbol@new1{SPY}, chart.setSymbol@new2{QQQ}. Never drop a ticker the member named ("open a QQQ chart" needs its chart.setSymbol). Types: chart (Chart), watchlist (Watchlist), themes (Theme Tracker), scanner (Scanner), fundamentals (Fundamentals), breadth (Breadth), aisearch (AI Search), news (News & Catalysts), notebook (Notebook), profile (Stock Profile), alerts (Alerts), calendar (UCT Terminal), optionsflow (Options Flow), nhnl (New Highs / Lows), nhnlPulse (H/L Pulse), volumescan (Volume Surge), scatter (Market Map).

m1.name: widget.addCharts
m1.summary: Add one NEW chart per symbol of an ordered list (tickers, a screen's results, or a saved watchlist), placed together in empty space. Existing widgets are never changed.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the workspace entry. symbols = the tickers, uppercase, OR {from, top} to chart a source's stocks in its order: from = the ref of a saved watchlist (its stocks, read fresh in its saved order when they apply), the "as" of a screener.run / screener.runSaved op in this request, or "lastScreen" for the last screen run here; top = how many charts (required, at most 12). timeframe: 1|5|15|30|60 minutes, D, W, M, or null to keep the default. chart_type: candles|hollow|bars|hlc|line|area or null. exact: true only if they insist on exactly that many (else fewer results just make fewer charts). Use this — not widget.add + chart.setSymbol — whenever the charts' symbols come from a screen or watchlist. Never type tickers you have not been given.

m1.name: screener.run
m1.summary: Run a stock screen on UCT's Screener and show the real matches (count + top rows). Changes nothing in UCT. Use this for "show me / find stocks with …".
m1.hints: target = the screener entry ref. filters: each {field: a key from screener `fields` (never invented), op, value, max, values}. Numbers: op gt|gte|lt|lte|eq|between, value, max (between only, else null), values null; % fields take 5 for 5%, $ fields take dollars (10M = 10000000). yes/no: op eq, value 1|0. (list) fields: op in|not_in, values = the member's own words (["software"]) — UCT matches the real values; value/max null. "(latest session)" fields only when a session is named ("today", "yesterday"); "$10M a day" / "per day" if none named = the 30-day average, not share volume. A measure not in `fields`: say the Screener doesn't have it, never substitute. sort_field/sort_dir or null. mode refine = change the LAST screen, else new. show: rows (null = 10, max 25). as: name the RESULT (screen1) when a later op uses its stocks ({from:"screen1", top:null} = all); else null. within: a watchlist ref only if they name that list ("in Momentum"); else null (the whole market).

m1.name: screener.runSaved
m1.summary: Run one of the member's saved screens (or a UCT starter screen) and show the real matches.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry; screen = the id of an entry in savedScreens (never invent one; clarify with the real names if unsure). show: rows (null = 10). as: name its RESULT when a later op in the same request uses its stocks; else null.

m1.name: screener.state
m1.summary: Say what the last screen run here was: its filters, sort and number of matches.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

m1.name: screener.listSaved
m1.summary: List the member's saved screens and UCT's starter screens.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

m1.name: screener.saveAs
m1.summary: Save the LAST screen run here (its exact filters, sort, ranking and logic) as a new saved screen in the member's Screener. Never replaces an existing one.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; name = the name as given. It saves the last screen run here — one run earlier in this conversation, or earlier in this same request. To run a NEW screen and save it in one request: the screen first, then this — it saves that screen.

m1.name: screener.duplicateSaved
m1.summary: Copy a saved screen (one of the member's or a UCT starter) to a new saved screen with exactly the same definition (filters, sort, ranking, logic, view, columns).
m1.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of the screen to copy (from yours, or a starter id from the screener entry's savedScreens); name = the new name as given, or null for "<name> copy" (do not ask for a name).

m1.name: screener.renameSaved
m1.summary: Rename one of the member's own saved screens.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens; name = the new name as given.

m1.name: screener.deleteSaved
m1.summary: Delete one of the member's own saved screens (permanent). UCT's starter screens cannot be deleted.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens. If more than one could be meant, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?".

m1.name: widget.remove
m1.summary: Remove a widget from the board (any type). Undo puts it back exactly — same place, size, link colour and settings. The space it leaves stays empty unless widget.arrange fills it.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of the widget from the board entry's widgets. If several could be meant, clarify — never guess.

m1.name: widget.move
m1.summary: Move and/or resize ONE widget to a rectangle on the board grid, exactly like dropping it there: the other widgets re-tile around it.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; x, y = the new top-left cell (columns from 0 at the left, rows from 0 at the top); w, h = the new width/height in cells, or null to keep the current size. The board entry gives the grid size and every widget's x/y/w/h. "to the left" = x 0; "narrower" = smaller w; "full height" = y 0 and h = rows.

m1.name: widget.arrange
m1.summary: Re-arrange widgets: "fill" grows them into the empty space around them (nothing else moves); "grid", "columns" or "rows" re-tile them evenly over the area they cover.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widgets = the ids to arrange, or null for every widget on the board; pattern = fill | grid | columns | rows. "make the remaining charts fill the space" = fill on those charts (after a widget.remove in the same plan).

m1.name: widget.setLink
m1.summary: Set a widget's link colour: widgets with the same colour follow the same symbol; N = not linked.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; color = A (gold), B (blue), C (green), D (purple), E (red), F (teal), G (orange), H (pink), N (not linked) — E–H only when the board entry says extraLinkColors: true. "Link these two charts" = give both the same colour (use one already on one of them).

m1.name: widget.showList
m1.summary: Make a Watchlist widget show one of the member's own watchlists (what picking it in the widget does).
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of a watchlist widget; list = the ref of the watchlist (from watchlists).

m1.name: widget.showScan
m1.summary: Make a Scanner widget show one of UCT's scans (what picking it in the widget does).
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of a scanner widget; scan = highest-volume-1y (Highest Volume In 1-Year), highest-volume-ever (Highest Volume Ever), ipo-1y (IPO in Last 1-Year), top-gainers-30d (Top Gainers (30-Day)), top-gainers-60d (Top Gainers (60-Day)), top-gainers-90d (Top Gainers (90-Day)).

m1.name: widget.resize
m1.summary: Resize ONE widget by moving one of its edges, exactly like dragging that edge: the widget the edge moves into shrinks (never below its minimum); nothing leaves the board.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; edge = left | right | top | bottom; by = cells to move the edge OUTWARD (positive = bigger, negative = smaller). "Make my watchlist narrower and give the chart more space" = resize the CHART toward the watchlist (the watchlist shrinks), or the watchlist inward then widget.arrange fill on the chart.

m1.name: widget.selectTab
m1.summary: Switch a widget to one of its tabs (clicking the tab in the widget header).
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; tab = "main" (the widget's own content), "1", "2"… or the tab's name, from the board entry's widgetTabs. NOT chart tabs (those are chart.*Tab).

m1.name: widget.renameTab
m1.summary: Rename one of a widget's tabs (double-click the tab), or clear the name back to the automatic label. At most 24 characters.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; tab = "main" (the widget's own content), "1", "2"… or the tab's name, from the board entry's widgetTabs. NOT chart tabs (those are chart.*Tab). name = the new name, or null to go back to the automatic label.

m1.name: widget.closeTab
m1.summary: Close one of a widget's extra tabs (its ×); the widget's own main tab cannot be closed. Undo puts the tab back exactly, settings included.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; tab = "main" (the widget's own content), "1", "2"… or the tab's name, from the board entry's widgetTabs. NOT chart tabs (those are chart.*Tab).

m1.name: widget.addTab
m1.summary: Add another widget as a TAB inside an existing (non-chart) widget — the widget header's "+" — and show it. Nothing else on the board moves. Undo closes it.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; type = one of chart, watchlist, themes, scanner, fundamentals, breadth, aisearch, news, notebook, profile, alerts, calendar, optionsflow, nhnl, nhnlPulse, volumescan, scatter. For a chart's own tabs (symbols, timeframes) use chart.addTab.

m1.name: indicator.list
m1.summary: List the indicators on ONE chart (as its legend names them): built-in or custom, shown or hidden, on the price chart or in its own pane. UCT answers from the chart's real state — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what indicators are on a chart, whether one is on, or which are hidden, instead of answering yourself.
m1.hints: target = the indicators entry for the chart the member means (with several charts and no chart named, ask which). filter: hidden | shown | null (all).

m1.name: indicator.add
m1.summary: Add ONE indicator to ONE chart — exactly what the Indicator Library's Add to Chart does. Built-in indicators or the member's own saved ones; Undo removes it again.
m1.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. defId = an id from indicatorCatalog (never invented, never a name). The SAME indicator on several charts = one indicator.add per chart named, same defId; if it isn't clear which charts, ask. Classic overlay averages (the legacy EMA/SMA rows) and Volume Profile are NOT added this way — say they live in Chart Settings. inputs = null for the indicator's defaults, else [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that row's `settings` ("a 20 EMA" → movingAverage, [{key:"period",value:20},{key:"maType",value:"ema"}]; "RSI 7" → rsi, [{key:"period",value:7}]). Every number or type the member named goes in inputs — never drop one or add a default instead. A setting the row does not list: say it isn't available; never guess a key. A moving average named by its LENGTH only ("the 9 and 20", "a 50 ma"): EMA for 8, 9, 10, 20 and 21, SMA for 50 and above (the member's default — say which you used); any other length: ask EMA or SMA.

m1.name: indicator.remove
m1.summary: Remove ONE indicator (its whole group, e.g. all COT panes) from ONE chart — the settings ✕ / legend Delete. Always shown as a proposal first, listing anything it would disconnect. Undo restores it exactly (same identity, reconnected inputs).
m1.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m1.name: indicator.update
m1.summary: Change the settings of ONE indicator already on ONE chart, in place — its length, its moving-average type, or another setting its row lists (what the indicator's settings dialog does). Never adds a second copy. Undo puts the old settings back.
m1.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). inputs = [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that indicator's settings, and ONLY the settings the member named — everything else stays as it is (an EMA stays an EMA unless they name a type). "make it a 9" right after adding an EMA 20 → that EMA, [{key:"period",value:9}]; "change that to an SMA" → [{key:"maType",value:"sma"}]. Use this — never indicator.remove + indicator.add — to change an indicator that is already on the chart.

m1.name: indicator.show
m1.summary: Show ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
m1.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m1.name: indicator.hide
m1.summary: Hide ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
m1.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m3.name: breadth.show
m3.summary: MARKET BREADTH from UCT's own data (US, NYSE, Nasdaq): now, on a date or at the close (a close not finalized yet is labelled provisional), the last N sessions, two dates compared, or a range — % above a moving average, new highs/lows, advance/decline, Stage 2/4. UCT shows the figures; you never see them. Use this (disposition apply, research null), never state breadth figures yourself.
m3.hints: target = breadth ref. universe us (default) | nyse | nasdaq | uct. metrics 1–4 keys; [] = general overview. value: date null = now; basis "close" if a close is asked; side "below" for % BELOW MA; else null. compare: compare_date. series: start, end null = latest. rows: sessions N = last N readings. Dates YYYY-MM-DD or null. reply: one short line, no figures. Keys: pct_above_{5,10,20,40,50,100,150,200}sma = % of stocks above that N-day simple MA; new_52w_highs/new_52w_lows = counts at 52-week highs/lows; net_new_high_low = highs minus lows; hi_ratio/lo_ratio = % of stocks at 52-week highs/lows; new_20d_highs/new_20d_lows = 20-day; near_52w_high = within 5% of 52w high; up_4pct_today/down_4pct_today = up/down 4%+ that day; ratio_5day/ratio_10day = up-4%/down-4% ratio over 5/10 days; adv_decline = net advancers; advancing/declining = issues up/down; universe_count = stocks counted; stage2_count/stage4_count = Stage 2 uptrend / Stage 4 downtrend counts.

m3.name: breadth.history
m3.summary: Search UCT's finalized daily MARKET BREADTH history (US, NYSE, Nasdaq) for when a condition held: the last/first time a measure was below/above a level, crossings, how many times, episodes and how long they lasted. UCT computes it and shows the member; you never see figures. Never say UCT lacks historical breadth.
m3.hints: target = breadth entry ref. universe us (default) | nyse | nasdaq | uct; metric = ONE key (same keys as breadth.show). op below | at_or_below | above | at_or_above (strict unless at_or) | crosses_below | crosses_above; level in the measure's unit (10 = 10%). find last | first (date of the most recent / earliest match) | count (sessions + episodes; crossings for crosses_*) | episodes | longest | last_episode (runs of consecutive sessions). start / end YYYY-MM-DD or null (all history). aggregation "daily". A follow-up "that" / "it" = the measure and universe of the member's last breadth request. Lowest / highest in a period: breadth.show mode series. reply: one short line, no figures.

m4.name: chart.setType
m4.summary: Change how price is drawn on one chart.

m4.name: chart.setTimeframe
m4.summary: Change one chart's timeframe.
m4.hints: Codes: 1, 5, 15, 30, 60 are minutes; D daily, W weekly, M monthly.

m4.name: chart.setSymbol
m4.summary: Show a different ticker on one chart. Widgets linked to the same color group follow, exactly as a manual symbol search does.

m4.name: chart.setSession
m4.summary: Show or hide pre/post-market (extended hours) on one chart.

m4.name: chart.setScale
m4.summary: Set one chart's price scale: linear (arithmetic), logarithmic, or percent.

m4.name: chart.applyTheme
m4.summary: Apply one of UCT's built-in chart color themes (canvas, candles, grid, text) to one chart.

m4.name: chart.setBackground
m4.summary: Set one chart's background to a single solid color.
m4.hints: Pass a hex color like #f3efe4; translate plain color names to hex.

m4.name: chart.setCandleColors
m4.summary: Set one chart's up and/or down candle colors.
m4.hints: Hex colors; pass null for a side that should not change.

m4.name: volume.setState
m4.summary: Show, hide, or remove one chart's built-in Volume pane.
m4.hints: "hide volume" is hidden (stays in the legend); "remove volume" is removed (off the chart).

m4.name: chart.setSetting
m4.summary: Change one chart display setting from UCT's approved list (grid and its color, crosshair and its color, scale text size/color, legend, watermark and its size/weight/lines, labels, event markers, swing labels and their options, prev-day lines and their style/width/color, countdown, title, color mode, thin bars, inverted scale).
m4.hints: value = true/false for on/off settings (crosshair.mode and header.legendMode also take true/false); a hex color (#2962ff) for color settings. Allowed values — crosshair.mode, header.legendMode: always|hold|off; textSize: 8|10|11|12|14|16|18|20|22|24|28|32|40; header.titleMode: ticker|company|both; candleColorMode: onecolor|netchange|openclose; swingLabels.sensitivity: low|medium|high; crosshair.width, prevDayLevels.high.width, prevDayLevels.low.width, prevDayLevels.close.width: 1|2|3|4; crosshair.style, prevDayLevels.high.style, prevDayLevels.low.style, prevDayLevels.close.style: solid|dashed|dotted; watermark.sizeScale: 0.5|0.75|1|1.25|1.5|2|2.5|3|4; watermark.weight: 300|400|500|600|700|800. Only these settings: for any other chart setting (watermark opacity, volume style…) do NOT plan an op — say it is not Agent-enabled yet and where it lives in Chart Settings.

m4.name: chart.applyTemplate
m4.summary: Apply one of the member's saved chart templates to ONE chart, exactly as clicking it does (Chart Settings → Templates, or right-click → Chart template): the chart takes the template's whole saved setup, its indicators included.
m4.hints: template = a name from chartTemplates, exactly. For several charts ("all my charts"), one op per chart.

m4.name: chart.resetDefaults
m4.summary: Restore ONE chart's look to UCT's defaults (Chart Settings → Restore defaults): colours, markers, header, watermark and display settings. The chart's indicators are kept exactly as they are.
m4.hints: target = the chart. Always shown as a proposal first.

m4.name: chart.goToDate
m4.summary: Scroll ONE chart so a past date is at its right edge — exactly the Time Navigator date box. A view change only: every bar stays on the chart (it is not a replay), nothing is saved; Undo scrolls back.
m4.hints: date = YYYY-MM-DD. "As it looked on <date>" = this (say in the reply that later bars are still there, just scrolled off to the right).

m4.name: chart.compare
m4.summary: Overlay other symbols on ONE chart (Tools → Compare Symbols): add tickers, remove some, or clear all comparisons.
m4.hints: add = tickers to overlay, uppercase ([] for none); remove = tickers to take off ([] for none); clear = true to remove every comparison. "Compare NVDA against QQQ on this chart" = target the NVDA chart, add [QQQ].

m4.name: chart.addCustomTimeframe
m4.summary: Add a custom timeframe (e.g. 45 minutes, 2 hours, 3 days) to ONE chart's timeframe menu, exactly like the menu's Custom interval, and optionally switch the chart to it.
m4.hints: unit = minutes | hours | days | weeks | months; count = how many (45 for 45 minutes); switch = true to show the chart on it now (the usual case), false to only add it to the menu.

m4.name: screener.run
m4.summary: Run a stock screen on UCT's Screener and show the real matches (count + top rows). Changes nothing in UCT. Use this for "show me / find stocks with …".
m4.hints: target = the screener entry ref. filters: each {field: a key from screener `fields` (never invented), op, value, max, values}. Numbers: op gt|gte|lt|lte|eq|between, value, max (between only, else null), values null; % fields take 5 for 5%, $ fields take dollars (10M = 10000000). yes/no: op eq, value 1|0. (list) fields: op in|not_in, values = the member's own words (["software"]) — UCT matches the real values; value/max null. "(latest session)" fields only when a session is named ("today", "yesterday"); "$10M a day" / "per day" if none named = the 30-day average, not share volume. A measure not in `fields`: say the Screener doesn't have it, never substitute. sort_field/sort_dir or null. mode refine = change the LAST screen, else new. show: rows (null = 10, max 25). as: name the RESULT (screen1) when a later op uses its stocks ({from:"screen1", top:null} = all); else null. within: a watchlist ref only if they name that list ("in Momentum"); else null (the whole market).

m4.name: screener.runSaved
m4.summary: Run one of the member's saved screens (or a UCT starter screen) and show the real matches.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry; screen = the id of an entry in savedScreens (never invent one; clarify with the real names if unsure). show: rows (null = 10). as: name its RESULT when a later op in the same request uses its stocks; else null.

m4.name: screener.state
m4.summary: Say what the last screen run here was: its filters, sort and number of matches.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

m4.name: screener.listSaved
m4.summary: List the member's saved screens and UCT's starter screens.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

m4.name: alert.list
m4.summary: Show the member's price alerts from UCT's real alert list: which are active, which went off (and when). Use this (disposition apply) for "show my alerts", "do I have an alert on NVDA?", "which alerts went off today?".
m4.hints: target = the ref of the alertLibrary entry. symbol: one ticker to filter by, or null. status: active | triggered | all, or null (= all). triggered_today: true only for "today"; else null. These are PRICE alerts only — indicator alerts (RSI, MACD…) are not listed here.

m4.name: alert.create
m4.summary: Create ONE price alert in UCT's Alerts: it goes off ONCE when the stock is at or above (direction above) or at or below (direction below) a price level, checked while the market is open. Only price levels — no percent-move, indicator, volume or time alerts; alerts cannot be paused, edited or made repeating.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the alertLibrary entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase; price = the level as a number; direction = above ("crosses above", "breaks above", "rises to", "gets to … from below") or below ("drops below", "falls to", "breaks down under"). If they give a level WITHOUT saying above or below (e.g. "an alert on NVDA at 200", "when it hits 200"), clarify with choices above / below — never guess. One op per alert, at most 5 in one request. An earlier alert at that level that already went off does NOT stop a new one — create it. Creating is always shown to the member as a proposal first, so plan it (disposition propose) — even inside a question ("why is TSLA moving? and set an alert above 300": propose the alert AND ask research for the question). For an alert on an indicator (RSI, MACD, a moving average…) or a percent move, use disposition unsupported: those are not price-level alerts.

m4.name: alert.delete
m4.summary: Delete one of the member's price alerts (permanent — UCT cannot restore a deleted alert).
m4.hints: target = the ref of that alert in the alerts list. One op per alert. Deleting is always shown to the member as a proposal first, so when the alert is clear (including "it" / "that one" right after an alert was named) plan the op — never ask "are you sure?". "All my inactive alerts" = one op per alert whose status is not active. If more than one alert could be the one they mean (e.g. two alerts on AMD), clarify with the real alerts as choices — never pick one. If the alerts list is not shown, use alert.list first.

m4.name: stock.profile
m4.summary: Answer a question about ONE stock's profile, price or fundamentals from UCT's own data: company name, sector/industry, price and today's change, market cap, P/E, 52-week range, revenue, margins, beta, next earnings date. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what's NVDA's market cap?", "what sector is AMD in?", "what's TSLA's P/E?" instead of answering from memory.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase. Not for news or "why is it moving" (that needs research).

m4.name: stock.earnings
m4.summary: Answer earnings questions about ONE stock from UCT's earnings data: the latest REPORTED quarter's revenue and EPS versus consensus estimates, year-over-year change, and the next report date with its estimates. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what was AMD's latest quarterly revenue?", "when does TSLA report earnings?", "did NVDA beat last quarter?".
m4.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase.

m4.name: stock.compare
m4.summary: Compare the fundamentals of TWO stocks side by side from UCT's Research data (market cap, P/E, revenue, growth, margins, beta, next earnings). Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "compare NVDA and AMD".
m4.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbols = exactly two tickers, uppercase. For three or more, clarify which two.

m4.name: breadth.show
m4.summary: MARKET BREADTH from UCT's own data (US, NYSE, Nasdaq): now, on a date or at the close (a close not finalized yet is labelled provisional), the last N sessions, two dates compared, or a range — % above a moving average, new highs/lows, advance/decline, Stage 2/4. UCT shows the figures; you never see them. Use this (disposition apply, research null), never state breadth figures yourself.
m4.hints: target = breadth ref. universe us (default) | nyse | nasdaq | uct. metrics 1–4 keys; [] = general overview. value: date null = now; basis "close" if a close is asked; side "below" for % BELOW MA; else null. compare: compare_date. series: start, end null = latest. rows: sessions N = last N readings. Dates YYYY-MM-DD or null. reply: one short line, no figures. Keys: pct_above_{5,10,20,40,50,100,150,200}sma = % of stocks above that N-day simple MA; new_52w_highs/new_52w_lows = counts at 52-week highs/lows; net_new_high_low = highs minus lows; hi_ratio/lo_ratio = % of stocks at 52-week highs/lows; new_20d_highs/new_20d_lows = 20-day; near_52w_high = within 5% of 52w high; up_4pct_today/down_4pct_today = up/down 4%+ that day; ratio_5day/ratio_10day = up-4%/down-4% ratio over 5/10 days; adv_decline = net advancers; advancing/declining = issues up/down; universe_count = stocks counted; stage2_count/stage4_count = Stage 2 uptrend / Stage 4 downtrend counts.

m4.name: breadth.history
m4.summary: Search UCT's finalized daily MARKET BREADTH history (US, NYSE, Nasdaq) for when a condition held: the last/first time a measure was below/above a level, crossings, how many times, episodes and how long they lasted. UCT computes it and shows the member; you never see figures. Never say UCT lacks historical breadth.
m4.hints: target = breadth entry ref. universe us (default) | nyse | nasdaq | uct; metric = ONE key (same keys as breadth.show). op below | at_or_below | above | at_or_above (strict unless at_or) | crosses_below | crosses_above; level in the measure's unit (10 = 10%). find last | first (date of the most recent / earliest match) | count (sessions + episodes; crossings for crosses_*) | episodes | longest | last_episode (runs of consecutive sessions). start / end YYYY-MM-DD or null (all history). aggregation "daily". A follow-up "that" / "it" = the measure and universe of the member's last breadth request. Lowest / highest in a period: breadth.show mode series. reply: one short line, no figures.

m4.name: settings.show
m4.summary: Say what the member's app settings are now (app theme, default chart timeframe, alert sound). Use this (disposition apply) for "show my settings".
m4.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry.

m4.name: settings.setAppTheme
m4.summary: Change the WHOLE APP's colour theme (sidebar, panels, pages) — e.g. "switch to dark mode / light mode". Not a chart's colours: for one chart use chart.applyTheme.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry. theme: dark = Graphite (the default dark), oled = OLED Black, light = Light; or one of UCT's themes: slate (Slate, dark), graphite (Graphite, dark), carbon (Carbon, dark), navy (Midnight Navy, dark), forest (Deep Forest, dark), espresso (Espresso, dark), plum (Plum, dark), nord (Nord, dark), gunmetal (Gunmetal, dark), bordeaux (Bordeaux, dark), storm (Storm, dark), umber (Umber, dark), paper (Paper, light), cream (Cream, light), coolgray (Cool Gray, light), softblue (Soft Blue, light), sand (Sand, light), mint (Mint, light). "Dark mode" = dark; "light mode" = light.

m4.name: settings.setDefaultTimeframe
m4.summary: Change the timeframe NEW charts open on by default (Settings → Charts). Charts already on the board keep theirs — for one of those use chart.setTimeframe.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry. timeframe: 5 | 30 | 60 (minutes), D (daily), W (weekly) — the only choices Settings offers.

m4.name: settings.setAlertSound
m4.summary: Turn the in-app alert sound on or off, and/or pick which sound plays (Settings → Preferences → Alerts). Does not change whether alerts are delivered.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry. enabled: true | false | null (keep); sound: chime (Chime), bell (Bell), ding (Ding), double_tap (Double Tap), triple_pop (Triple Pop), radar (Radar), urgent (Urgent), soft (Soft), pulse (Pulse), major (Major Chord), or null (keep).

m4.name: app.open
m4.summary: Open another UCT page for the member, exactly like clicking it in the sidebar: the Screener, Dashboard, Breadth, Settings, a stock's Research page, etc. This closes this panel (the conversation is kept).
m4.hints: target = the ref of the app entry. page: one of terminal (UCT Terminal), charts (Charts), morning-wire (Morning Wire), dashboard (Dashboard), ai-search (AI Search), uct-20 (UCT 20), breadth (Breadth), screener (Screener), options-flow (Options Flow), flow-scoreboard (Flow Record), live-massive (Live Flow), catalysts-history (Catalysts History), model-book (Model Book), formulas-reference (Formula Reference), desk (The Desk), journal (Journal), portfolio-heat (Portfolio Risk), community (Community), support (Support), settings (Settings), research (Research). section: only for page settings — account | billing | preferences | charts | compass | connections | legal — else null. symbol: only for page research (the ticker) — else null. Use this only when they ask to GO somewhere ("open / take me to / go to"); a question about data is answered here instead. Watchlists and Theme Tracker live on Charts (this page).

m4.name: news.latest
m4.summary: Show the latest news headlines UCT has stored for ONE stock (the Company Panel's News tab), each with time, source and tone. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "show me the latest NVDA news", "what news is UCT showing for PLTR".
m4.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase; limit = how many headlines (null = 8, at most 15). For WHY a stock is moving right now, or a summary of today's news across the web, use research instead. To compare two stocks' news, one op per stock.

m4.name: news.catalysts
m4.summary: Show the catalysts UCT's catalyst engine has recorded for ONE stock (the Catalysts History page): the days it was flagged, catalyst type, grade, gap and the thesis written at the time. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what are the recent catalysts for AMD?". UCT has no calendar of future events besides earnings (use stock.earnings for the next report).
m4.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase.

m4.name: settings.setWatchlistDigest
m4.summary: Turn the member's watchlist EMAIL digest (a performance summary of their watchlists, emailed to their account email) on — daily or weekly — or off. Same as Settings → Email Digest.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the watchlistDigest entry; frequency = daily (every day 5 PM ET) | weekly (Fridays 5 PM ET) | off. Turning it on starts recurring emails: plan it (propose) and say so in the reply. To just see the current setting, answer from the watchlistDigest entry.

m4.name: screener.saveAs
m4.summary: Save the LAST screen run here (its exact filters, sort, ranking and logic) as a new saved screen in the member's Screener. Never replaces an existing one.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; name = the name as given. It saves the last screen run here — one run earlier in this conversation, or earlier in this same request. To run a NEW screen and save it in one request: the screen first, then this — it saves that screen.

m4.name: screener.duplicateSaved
m4.summary: Copy a saved screen (one of the member's or a UCT starter) to a new saved screen with exactly the same definition (filters, sort, ranking, logic, view, columns).
m4.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of the screen to copy (from yours, or a starter id from the screener entry's savedScreens); name = the new name as given, or null for "<name> copy" (do not ask for a name).

m4.name: screener.renameSaved
m4.summary: Rename one of the member's own saved screens.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens; name = the new name as given.

m4.name: screener.deleteSaved
m4.summary: Delete one of the member's own saved screens (permanent). UCT's starter screens cannot be deleted.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens. If more than one could be meant, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?".

m4.name: chartGrid.set
m4.summary: Show these tickers as that many charts, in equal cells: the charts already on the board are reused (top-left first), any still needed are ADDED, and the charts' area is re-tiled as an even grid. Other widgets stay where they are; nothing is removed. One change, one Undo.
m4.hints: Use for "create/open/show N charts for A, B, C…", "put SPY, QQQ, NVDA and TSLA in a 2x2 grid", "show NVDA and AMD side by side" — whenever the member names the tickers for several charts. target = the ref of the board entry. symbols = the tickers in the member's order, uppercase. timeframe = the one timeframe they gave for all of them (1|5|15|30|60 minutes, D, W, M), else null. layout = "columns" for side by side, "rows" for stacked, "grid" for a grid, else null. new_charts = true only when they ask for NEW charts ("in new charts", "add four new charts") — the charts already there then keep their tickers; else null. watchlist = true when they also ask for a watchlist beside the charts ("…, and a watchlist") and the board has no Watchlist widget: a column on the right is cleared of charts and a Watchlist widget is added there; else null. replace = true only when the member chose to replace the current board with this workspace; else null. Never widget.add + chart.setSymbol for this.

m4.name: chart.applyThemeAll
m4.summary: Apply one of UCT's chart themes to EVERY chart on the board (and chart tabs), exactly as the theme gallery's "all charts" does; new charts on this layout start with it.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; theme = a chart theme id (the same ids as chart.applyTheme). For ONE chart use chart.applyTheme.

m4.name: chart.addTab
m4.summary: Add a new chart TAB to a chart widget (the tab strip's "+"), on the same link colour as the tab showing now, and switch to it.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; timeframe = 1|5|15|30|60|D|W|M or null (daily); name = a label for the tab or null. The new tab follows the same symbol until its link colour is changed (chart.linkTab).

m4.name: chart.selectTab
m4.summary: Switch a chart widget to one of its tabs (clicking the tab).
m4.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs.

m4.name: chart.closeTab
m4.summary: Close one EXTRA tab of a chart widget (its settings go with it; Undo brings it back exactly). The main tab cannot be closed.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs.

m4.name: chart.renameTab
m4.summary: Rename a chart widget's tab (double-click on the tab).
m4.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs. name = the new label (24 characters at most).

m4.name: chart.linkTab
m4.summary: Set the link colour of one chart TAB (the tab's colour dot): tabs and widgets with the same colour follow the same symbol.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs. color = A (gold), B (blue), C (green), D (purple), E (red), F (teal), G (orange), H (pink) (E–H only when the board entry says extraLinkColors: true) — a tab is always linked to a colour. "Two tabs with linked symbols" = give both the same colour.

m4.name: indicator.list
m4.summary: List the indicators on ONE chart (as its legend names them): built-in or custom, shown or hidden, on the price chart or in its own pane. UCT answers from the chart's real state — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what indicators are on a chart, whether one is on, or which are hidden, instead of answering yourself.
m4.hints: target = the indicators entry for the chart the member means (with several charts and no chart named, ask which). filter: hidden | shown | null (all).

m4.name: indicator.add
m4.summary: Add ONE indicator to ONE chart — exactly what the Indicator Library's Add to Chart does. Built-in indicators or the member's own saved ones; Undo removes it again.
m4.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. defId = an id from indicatorCatalog (never invented, never a name). The SAME indicator on several charts = one indicator.add per chart named, same defId; if it isn't clear which charts, ask. Classic overlay averages (the legacy EMA/SMA rows) and Volume Profile are NOT added this way — say they live in Chart Settings. inputs = null for the indicator's defaults, else [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that row's `settings` ("a 20 EMA" → movingAverage, [{key:"period",value:20},{key:"maType",value:"ema"}]; "RSI 7" → rsi, [{key:"period",value:7}]). Every number or type the member named goes in inputs — never drop one or add a default instead. A setting the row does not list: say it isn't available; never guess a key. A moving average named by its LENGTH only ("the 9 and 20", "a 50 ma"): EMA for 8, 9, 10, 20 and 21, SMA for 50 and above (the member's default — say which you used); any other length: ask EMA or SMA.

m4.name: indicator.remove
m4.summary: Remove ONE indicator (its whole group, e.g. all COT panes) from ONE chart — the settings ✕ / legend Delete. Always shown as a proposal first, listing anything it would disconnect. Undo restores it exactly (same identity, reconnected inputs).
m4.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m4.name: indicator.update
m4.summary: Change the settings of ONE indicator already on ONE chart, in place — its length, its moving-average type, or another setting its row lists (what the indicator's settings dialog does). Never adds a second copy. Undo puts the old settings back.
m4.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). inputs = [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that indicator's settings, and ONLY the settings the member named — everything else stays as it is (an EMA stays an EMA unless they name a type). "make it a 9" right after adding an EMA 20 → that EMA, [{key:"period",value:9}]; "change that to an SMA" → [{key:"maType",value:"sma"}]. Use this — never indicator.remove + indicator.add — to change an indicator that is already on the chart.

m4.name: indicator.show
m4.summary: Show ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
m4.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m4.name: indicator.hide
m4.summary: Hide ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
m4.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m4.name: agent.capabilities
m4.summary: Answer what UCT Agent can and cannot do (now, partly, not yet, planned) about a topic — from UCT's own capability list, never from memory.
m4.hints: target = the ref of the agent entry. Use ONLY for a question ABOUT abilities ("can you draw trendlines?", "what can you do with layouts?", "can you backtest?"). A polite request to DO something you can do ("can you switch this to weekly?") is a command: plan it, do not use this. topic: overview for "what can you do?"; other when no topic fits.

m4.name: guide.explain
m4.summary: Explain what a UCT term, indicator or feature IS (“what does ADR mean?”, “explain RSI”, “the difference between an indicator and a condition”), from UCT's own catalog. Changes nothing.
m4.hints: target = the guide entry. topic = the member's words for what to explain (an indicator, a UCT term or feature). Prefer it for UCT's own indicators and features — its text is UCT's catalog. Use ONLY for "what is / what does / explain / difference" questions; a request to change something is a command — plan it.

m4.name: guide.show
m4.summary: SHOW the member where a Charts control is: highlight the real control on their board with a short step-by-step card (Next / Back / Exit). Changes nothing — use it for "where do I…", "show me how to…", "how do I…" questions, never to do the thing.
m4.hints: target = the guide entry. feature = one of: canvas (chart background, grid, crosshair and watermark); link (linking charts and widgets); symbol (changing a chart’s symbol); timeframe (changing the timeframe); indicators (adding and configuring an indicator); charts (creating and arranging several charts); watchlists (using watchlists); layouts (saving and switching layouts); hideDrawings (hiding and showing drawings); drawing (basic drawing tools); settings (finding chart settings). A request to DO it ("change my chart to weekly") is a command, not this.

m5.name: chart.setType
m5.summary: Change how price is drawn on one chart.

m5.name: chart.setTimeframe
m5.summary: Change one chart's timeframe.
m5.hints: Codes: 1, 5, 15, 30, 60 are minutes; D daily, W weekly, M monthly.

m5.name: chart.setSymbol
m5.summary: Show a different ticker on one chart. Widgets linked to the same color group follow, exactly as a manual symbol search does.

m5.name: chart.setSession
m5.summary: Show or hide pre/post-market (extended hours) on one chart.

m5.name: chart.setScale
m5.summary: Set one chart's price scale: linear (arithmetic), logarithmic, or percent.

m5.name: chart.applyTheme
m5.summary: Apply one of UCT's built-in chart color themes (canvas, candles, grid, text) to one chart.

m5.name: chart.setBackground
m5.summary: Set one chart's background to a single solid color.
m5.hints: Pass a hex color like #f3efe4; translate plain color names to hex.

m5.name: chart.setCandleColors
m5.summary: Set one chart's up and/or down candle colors.
m5.hints: Hex colors; pass null for a side that should not change.

m5.name: volume.setState
m5.summary: Show, hide, or remove one chart's built-in Volume pane.
m5.hints: "hide volume" is hidden (stays in the legend); "remove volume" is removed (off the chart).

m5.name: chart.setSetting
m5.summary: Change one chart display setting from UCT's approved list (grid and its color, crosshair and its color, scale text size/color, legend, watermark and its size/weight/lines, labels, event markers, swing labels and their options, prev-day lines and their style/width/color, countdown, title, color mode, thin bars, inverted scale).
m5.hints: value = true/false for on/off settings (crosshair.mode and header.legendMode also take true/false); a hex color (#2962ff) for color settings. Allowed values — crosshair.mode, header.legendMode: always|hold|off; textSize: 8|10|11|12|14|16|18|20|22|24|28|32|40; header.titleMode: ticker|company|both; candleColorMode: onecolor|netchange|openclose; swingLabels.sensitivity: low|medium|high; crosshair.width, prevDayLevels.high.width, prevDayLevels.low.width, prevDayLevels.close.width: 1|2|3|4; crosshair.style, prevDayLevels.high.style, prevDayLevels.low.style, prevDayLevels.close.style: solid|dashed|dotted; watermark.sizeScale: 0.5|0.75|1|1.25|1.5|2|2.5|3|4; watermark.weight: 300|400|500|600|700|800. A moving average named by its LENGTH only ("the 9 and 20", "a 50 ma"): EMA for 8, 9, 10, 20 and 21, SMA for 50 and above (the member's default — say which you used); any other length: ask EMA or SMA.

m7.name: indicator.remove
m7.summary: Remove ONE indicator (its whole group, e.g. all COT panes) from ONE chart — the settings ✕ / legend Delete. Always shown as a proposal first, listing anything it would disconnect. Undo restores it exactly (same identity, reconnected inputs).
m7.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m7.name: indicator.update
m7.summary: Change the settings of ONE indicator already on ONE chart, in place — its length, its moving-average type, or another setting its row lists (what the indicator's settings dialog does). Never adds a second copy. Undo puts the old settings back.
m7.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). inputs = [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that indicator's settings, and ONLY the settings the member named — everything else stays as it is (an EMA stays an EMA unless they name a type). "make it a 9" right after adding an EMA 20 → that EMA, [{key:"period",value:9}]; "change that to an SMA" → [{key:"maType",value:"sma"}]. Use this — never indicator.remove + indicator.add — to change an indicator that is already on the chart.

m7.name: indicator.show
m7.summary: Show ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
m7.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m7.name: indicator.hide
m7.summary: Hide ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
m7.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m7.name: agent.capabilities
m7.summary: Answer what UCT Agent can and cannot do (now, partly, not yet, planned) about a topic — from UCT's own capability list, never from memory.
m7.hints: target = the ref of the agent entry. Use ONLY for a question ABOUT abilities ("can you draw trendlines?", "what can you do with layouts?", "can you backtest?"). A polite request to DO something you can do ("can you switch this to weekly?") is a command: plan it, do not use this. topic: overview for "what can you do?"; other when no topic fits.

m8.name: screener.run
m8.summary: Run a stock screen on UCT's Screener and show the real matches (count + top rows). Changes nothing in UCT. Use this for "show me / find stocks with …".
m8.hints: target = the screener entry ref. filters: each {field: a key from screener `fields` (never invented), op, value, max, values}. Numbers: op gt|gte|lt|lte|eq|between, value, max (between only, else null), values null; % fields take 5 for 5%, $ fields take dollars (10M = 10000000). yes/no: op eq, value 1|0. (list) fields: op in|not_in, values = the member's own words (["software"]) — UCT matches the real values; value/max null. "(latest session)" fields only when a session is named ("today", "yesterday"); "$10M a day" / "per day" if none named = the 30-day average, not share volume. A measure not in `fields`: say the Screener doesn't have it, never substitute. sort_field/sort_dir or null. mode refine = change the LAST screen, else new. show: rows (null = 10, max 25). as: name the RESULT (screen1) when a later op uses its stocks ({from:"screen1", top:null} = all); else null. within: a watchlist ref only if they name that list ("in Momentum"); else null (the whole market).

m8.name: screener.runSaved
m8.summary: Run one of the member's saved screens (or a UCT starter screen) and show the real matches.
m8.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry; screen = the id of an entry in savedScreens (never invent one; clarify with the real names if unsure). show: rows (null = 10). as: name its RESULT when a later op in the same request uses its stocks; else null.

m8.name: screener.state
m8.summary: Say what the last screen run here was: its filters, sort and number of matches.
m8.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

m8.name: screener.listSaved
m8.summary: List the member's saved screens and UCT's starter screens.
m8.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

m8.name: stock.profile
m8.summary: Answer a question about ONE stock's profile, price or fundamentals from UCT's own data: company name, sector/industry, price and today's change, market cap, P/E, 52-week range, revenue, margins, beta, next earnings date. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what's NVDA's market cap?", "what sector is AMD in?", "what's TSLA's P/E?" instead of answering from memory.
m8.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase. Not for news or "why is it moving" (that needs research).

m8.name: stock.earnings
m8.summary: Answer earnings questions about ONE stock from UCT's earnings data: the latest REPORTED quarter's revenue and EPS versus consensus estimates, year-over-year change, and the next report date with its estimates. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what was AMD's latest quarterly revenue?", "when does TSLA report earnings?", "did NVDA beat last quarter?".
m8.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase.

m8.name: stock.compare
m8.summary: Compare the fundamentals of TWO stocks side by side from UCT's Research data (market cap, P/E, revenue, growth, margins, beta, next earnings). Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "compare NVDA and AMD".
m8.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbols = exactly two tickers, uppercase. For three or more, clarify which two.

m8.name: news.latest
m8.summary: Show the latest news headlines UCT has stored for ONE stock (the Company Panel's News tab), each with time, source and tone. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "show me the latest NVDA news", "what news is UCT showing for PLTR".
m8.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase; limit = how many headlines (null = 8, at most 15). For WHY a stock is moving right now, or a summary of today's news across the web, use research instead. To compare two stocks' news, one op per stock.

m8.name: news.catalysts
m8.summary: Show the catalysts UCT's catalyst engine has recorded for ONE stock (the Catalysts History page): the days it was flagged, catalyst type, grade, gap and the thesis written at the time. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what are the recent catalysts for AMD?". UCT has no calendar of future events besides earnings (use stock.earnings for the next report).
m8.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase.

m8.name: screener.saveAs
m8.summary: Save the LAST screen run here (its exact filters, sort, ranking and logic) as a new saved screen in the member's Screener. Never replaces an existing one.
m8.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; name = the name as given. It saves the last screen run here — one run earlier in this conversation, or earlier in this same request. To run a NEW screen and save it in one request: the screen first, then this — it saves that screen.

m8.name: screener.duplicateSaved
m8.summary: Copy a saved screen (one of the member's or a UCT starter) to a new saved screen with exactly the same definition (filters, sort, ranking, logic, view, columns).
m8.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of the screen to copy (from yours, or a starter id from the screener entry's savedScreens); name = the new name as given, or null for "<name> copy" (do not ask for a name).

m8.name: screener.renameSaved
m8.summary: Rename one of the member's own saved screens.
m8.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens; name = the new name as given.

m8.name: screener.deleteSaved
m8.summary: Delete one of the member's own saved screens (permanent). UCT's starter screens cannot be deleted.
m8.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens. If more than one could be meant, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?".

m8.name: agent.capabilities
m8.summary: Answer what UCT Agent can and cannot do (now, partly, not yet, planned) about a topic — from UCT's own capability list, never from memory.
m8.hints: target = the ref of the agent entry. Use ONLY for a question ABOUT abilities ("can you draw trendlines?", "what can you do with layouts?", "can you backtest?"). A polite request to DO something you can do ("can you switch this to weekly?") is a command: plan it, do not use this. topic: overview for "what can you do?"; other when no topic fits.
